reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - donanemab achieved 87.03 centiloid reduction in amyloid PET signal vs 0.67 in placebo (p<0.0001), demonstrating robust amyloid plaque clearance. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed pathway effects - while amyloid plaques were cleared as intended, tau PET showed no significant difference (p=0.4522), and there was concerning accelerated brain volume loss (-6.66 cm³ difference) and ventricular expansion (3.02 cm³ difference). This suggests the amyloid clearance pathway was engaged but with complex downstream effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with statistical significance - iADRS showed 2.92 point difference (p=0.001), supported by secondary endpoints MMSE (0.47 difference, p=0.012) and ADAS-Cog13 (-1.33 difference, p=0.0006). Effect sizes are clinically meaningful for Alzheimer's disease. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Intermediate tau population showed enhanced benefit (3.25 vs 2.92 point iADRS difference), suggesting biomarker-defined subgroups may respond better. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues - adequate sample size (1736), appropriate duration (76 weeks), placebo-controlled design. Some safety signals including cardiac events and brain volume changes, but these did not prevent efficacy demonstration.

failure_modes.evidence: Accelerated brain volume loss and ventricular expansion raise questions about long-term safety profile, though these did not prevent completion of the efficacy trial
